newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: El Nino causes water shortage for Guatemalan crops.
newsitem.headline: El Nino causes water shortage for Guatemalan crops.

text.p: Guatemalan officials said the El Nino weather phenomenon has caused drought and would harm crops such as corn and dry beans and maybe even hit coffee plantations.
To date, the Agriculture Ministry officials said they did not have details on losses, nor forecasts.

"It has caused a rain deficit in the southwest, the southeast and the central mesa. There is a 45 percent rain deficit (for April through July) in the southeast," Mario Bautista, of the National Seismology, Vulcanology and Meteorology Institute told Reuters.
El Nino, a warm current in the Pacific Ocean, affects weather patterns in countries all around the Pacific Rim.
According to Bautista several larger corn growers along Guatemala's Pacific coast have reported harvest losses.
"Specific percentages of loss are impossible for us to generate because the the phenomenon is so rapid and is subject to variations," said Isabel Prieto, spokeswoman for the Agriculture Ministry
Prieto said the grains most susceptible to loss were corn and dry beans.
Bautista said rains are more regular in most of the coffee-growing areas, but he said some big coffee growers in the southwest have reported a lack of water.
Julio Arrivillaga, president of the National Coffee Association, said the most risky months for coffee growers would be when coffee plants are flowering from November to March.
"If there is a serious drought in the dry season, which goes from November to May, we won't have flowers and that reduces the harvest," Arrivillaga said.
Very few coffee farms have any kind of irrigation systems, he said.
"I would say there is a large risk, but we have to wait. We are fearful there won't be rain during those months," Arrivillaga said.

Prieto said the ministry was planning actions to counteract the impact of El Nino, including identifying risk areas, advice for growers of vulnerable crops, suggesting alternative crops, pest control, and funding to rehabilitate wells and pumps.
Guatemala has no plans to limit grains exports, she said. Honduras recently slapped a temporary ban on corn and beans exports because of fears of national shortages.
